question: What is the meaning of toxic material according to reach in relation to safety, health, environmental hygiene?
description: Toxic materials are substances that pose a risk to safety, health, and environmental hygiene. They can cause cancer, genetic mutations, impair fertility, harm unborn children, interfere with the endocrine system, target and damage specific organs, affect respiratory health, cause skin sensitization or allergic reactions, persist in the environment, accumulate in living organisms, and contribute to ozone depletion. These materials are also hazardous to aquatic life and the ozone layer. They negatively affect the reuse and recycling of materials, hinder recycling processes, and take up more than 0.1% of the product's weight. Exemptions might apply if sharing the information is difficult due to technicalities or other reasons. No exceptions can apply if the substance of concern takes up more than 0.1% of the product's weight.
